neighbours.label: the subject or verb inside a relative clause about a role or activity someone kept up over time ('a position he held until', 'which they ran', 'that he continued to operate', 'committees she served on')
fire: In 1931 he was named head coach, a post he kept until the war began.
They opened a small inn, which they managed together for thirty years.
She took over the family farm, which she continued to work until 1960.
He was elected mayor, an office he occupied for three full terms.
The boards he has sat on include two hospitals and a university.
After the war she founded a newspaper that she edited until her death.
He became choir director, a role that he filled until his retirement.
The brothers started a shipping firm, which they ran from a tiny office.
quiet: In 1931 he was named head coach, and the team won its first title.
They opened a small inn near the harbor in the summer of 1902.
She took over the family farm when her father fell ill in 1935.
He was elected mayor by a narrow margin after a bitter race.
The hospital and the university are both located on the same street.
After the war she moved to Paris and studied painting for a year.
He became choir director in the autumn after the old one moved away.
The brothers bought a ship and sailed it to the island in the spring.
